accepted_claims: For finite simple undirected loopless graphs, unit initial counts and arbitrary positive vertex rates, surviving support is almost surely a forest for alpha > 4/3.
Any even cycle forces strict linear instability for alpha > 1; an odd m-cycle does so for alpha > sec^2(pi/(2m)), with arbitrary positive rates, nonuniform weights and attachments.
For equal positive rates, surviving support is almost surely a whisker forest for alpha >= 17/4, meaning every component is a tree of diameter at most three.
The equal-rate triangle is strictly stable and attained with positive probability from unit initial counts for 1 < alpha < 4/3; this known obstruction makes the forest lower threshold sharp.
The exact unequal-rate diameter-four path at alpha = 2 is a strictly stable, stochastically attainable scope control outside the equal-rate whisker hypothesis.
